definition_sections.retitled_item: Responsibilities item 3: UI Verification: Live Browser and Desktop Application UAT

amendments.section: ## Desktop UAT Testing > ### Launch the tested artifact
amendments.reason: close-app cannot resolve a hosted application. --app resolves against list-apps, where a hosted application appears under its host process, so close-app answers APP_NOT_FOUND while list-windows --app finds the window. Verified against CalculatorApp.exe on this host. The section now records the window Close ref route.

sections: ## Desktop UAT Testing > ### The observe, act, verify loop
## Desktop UAT Testing > ### Windows and PowerShell specifics
## Desktop UAT Testing > ### What to assert
amendments.reason: The .ps1 shim drops the pipeline and certifies an empty value as delivered. agent-desktop resolves to agent-desktop.ps1, which is a thin wrapper over the native executable, and PowerShell does not forward a script's pipeline into a native command, so --stdin reached the tool as EOF; the tool wrote an empty value, read it back empty, and returned ok true with delivered_verified. The .cmd and native routes deliver the value but answer ACTION_FAILED with no value in post_state, a false negative. get reads one named property and never reports available_actions. snapshot --app silently takes the focused window when an application has several windows instead of raising AMBIGUOUS_TARGET. wait --text cannot match a value held in a control. All four measured against agent-desktop 1.3.1 on this host.

amendments.section: ## Desktop UAT Testing > ### Windows and PowerShell specifics
amendments.reason: The claim was over-broad. It said snapshot --app never raises AMBIGUOUS_TARGET for a multi-window application and silently takes the focused window. The rc.002 run measured both halves: with several windows and one of them focused the tool returns ok true on that window and emits no error block, and with several windows and none focused it raises AMBIGUOUS_TARGET and names the candidate window ids. The bullet now states both cases and keeps the operative rule unchanged, which was always right: pin --window-id taken from list-windows --app whenever more than one window exists, rather than reading the envelope to discover which behaviour you got. The old sentence about the case that does raise the error is folded into the same bullet.

sections: ## Desktop UAT Testing > ### The observe, act, verify loop
## Desktop UAT Testing > ### Launch the tested artifact
amendments.reason: Two contract level hazards measured in the rc.004 run, neither of which the definition warned about. A saved ref can resolve onto an identical sibling instead of raising STALE_REF: with two Notepad windows open, a Close Tab ref captured from one snapshot was acted on after its own tab had been removed, the act returned ok true and InvokePattern.Invoke succeeded, and the click landed on the identical Close Tab in the sibling window, closing that window's document. The clean case does raise STALE_REF with details.kind saved_ref_absent, so the fresh snapshot advice stands while its implied guarantee does not, and the section now states that a successful act is not proof the ref addressed the intended node. Separately, closing a window whose document has unsaved changes discards that work with no prompt while returning ok true and delivered_verified, verified twice on this host through the positional close-app and through the window's own Close ref. Both hazards were added as two bullets and nothing else in the definition changed.
